summary: One scrip code on three instruments (audit RB-03): ITC on NSE cash, BSE cash and an NSE future all carry 1660, and each frame reaches only the instrument its Exch, ExchType and Token name; unsubscribing BSE releases only BSE, and NSE still holds its own last price.

notes: The NSE frames are the web test's FEED (and FEED with LastRate 0); the BSE and NFO frames are worked here with their own prices, so a price borrowed across instruments shows.
One token on NSE cash, BSE cash and NSE F&O is the audit's scenario; real scrip codes differ per exchange more often than not.

deviations.reason: data.mode is the label every broker's frames carry on the desktop (ltp, quote, full), as the recorded Zerodha transcripts carry it; this web adapter puts its subscription mode number there.

The web passes 5paisa's JSON number on as it came, so a whole price (the web test's OpenRate 445) goes out as an integer (445); the desktop sends every price as a float (445.0), as the docs' frames (docs/prompt/websockets-format.md) and every other broker's prices are. Same value, other JSON type.

The web sends 5paisa's ChgPcnt as percent_change for every instrument; the desktop's common carrier sends the change fields for indices only, so an equity or a future loses it. Carrier gap (change fields for every exchange, audit C04, lane wire).
The web's Quote sends 5paisa's best bid (BidRate); the desktop's common carrier has no best bid or ask. Carrier gap (audit C06, lane wire).
The web's Quote sends 5paisa's best bid quantity (BidQty); the desktop's common carrier has no best bid or ask. Carrier gap (audit C06, lane wire).
The web's Quote sends 5paisa's best ask (OffRate); the desktop's common carrier has no best bid or ask. Carrier gap (audit C06, lane wire).
The web's Quote sends 5paisa's best ask quantity (OffQty); the desktop's common carrier has no best bid or ask. Carrier gap (audit C06, lane wire).
